summary: As domestic monopolies grow into global giants, they form international cartels to divide world markets and avoid competing against one another.
context: Lenin traces how national monopolies in oil, electrical equipment, and shipping form international agreements to set global prices, allocate market territories, and eliminate independent competitors.

targetText:
This is a new stage of world concentration of capital and
 production, incomparably higher than the preceding stages.
summary: Capital concentration expands beyond national borders, creating multinational megacorporations that carve up global industries.
context: Global supply chains and transnational corporate alliances mark a new historical phase where corporate power operates above individual nation-states.

targetText: based on the economic division of the world
summary: International cartels divide the world into economic spheres of influence, where each cartel claims exclusive rights to sell goods and extract resources in designated countries.
context: This economic partition of the world lays the foundation for political and military conflicts, as imperialist nations step in to defend or expand their domestic cartels' global territories.
